Lydia of Thyatira: A Key Convert to Christianity in Europe

Lydia of Thyatira, born in the 1st century CE, is the first documented convert to Christianity in Europe. Her conversion is believed to have occurred during the reign of Emperor Domitian (81-96 CE), and she is often referred to as the first Christian martyr.

As a devout Christian, Lydia played a significant role in the early Christian community in Thyatira, where she is said to have founded a church. Her faith and influence helped to establish Christianity as a major force in the region, paving the way for the spread of the faith throughout Europe.

Lydia's legacy extends beyond her own lifetime, as she became a model for future Christian converts and a symbol of faith in the face of persecution. Her story has been passed down through the centuries, inspiring countless works of art, literature, and music.

In 2019, a team of archaeologists discovered a ancient baptistery in Thyatira, which is believed to be the site where Lydia was baptized. The discovery was a significant find, shedding new light on the life and legacy of this important figure in Christian history.
